newsitem.title: GERMANY: Protect Internet from pirates - Book Fair chief.
newsitem.headline: Protect Internet from pirates - Book Fair chief.

text.p: The chairman of the world's largest book fair called on Tuesday for tougher international laws to stop wholesale plundering of the Internet.

"Digital highways can only function if the necessary traffic regulations are provided," Roland Ulmer said at a news conference to launch the Frankfurt Fair that has attracted more than 9,000 publishers from 110 countries.
Owners of copyright risked exposing their intellectual property to unauthorised downloading, he said.

"Uncertainty on this sector is obstructing the commitment of economic resources. A new legal framework is urgently required," he added at the fair which is staging the first ever auction for Internet rights.
Literary agents plan to sell the rights to "Circle of Friends," the best-selling novel by Irish writer Maeve Binchy, at the fair which has taken Ireland as its main theme this year.
The auction is aimed largely at telecommunications firms who cannot publish texts owned by conventional publishers.
The German Booksellers and Publishers Association, urging much tighter control of a fast-expanding global market, proposed several ways of curbing Internet pirates.

Ulmer, presenting their findings, said the hardware industry "must develop systems which monitor and control access to database contents and make it possible to charge for this at individually determined prices."
He said protection rights were vital as digital technology now permitted almost unhindered access to the end user.
He suggested that existing international and national copyright laws should be used as a base for a new set of rules to curb the electronic plunderers.
Electronic publishing is a prime attraction at the week-long Frankfurt Fair.
